amendments.rule: **A verb the ASV renders as a light verb plus a complement heads on the complement, not on the light verb.** This is rule 31's test applied to a verb: drop each word in turn, and the head is the one whose loss loses the lexeme. `הַאֲזִין` → *Give ear unto* heads on *ear*, because *give* alone gives anything; so too `הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה` → *did obeisance*, `נוֹעַץ` → *took counsel*, `הִמְלִיךְ` → *make king*, `הוֹדָה` → *give thanks*, `כִּלָּה` → *made an end*, `עוּד` → *bear witness*, `חָנַן` → *make supplication*, `בּוֹשׁ` → *put to shame*. The complement need not be a noun: an adjective (`הִכְבִּיד` → *made heavy*, `גָּדַל` → *make greater*) and a second verb (`חָטָא` hiphil → *made to sin*, `אָכַל` → *did eat*) are read the same way. Rule 24's *lexical predicate over subjects and auxiliaries* is about `was gathered`, and must not be read as a preference for the English verb — that reasoning would head *make king* on *make*. **A phrasal particle is not a complement.** `שָׁלַח` → *put forth*, `סוּר` → *take away*, and `נָתַן` → *put away* are one lexical verb plus its particle, and the head stays on the verb; the same subtraction says so, since *forth* and *away* alone name nothing. **A supplied object is not a complement either.** Where the ASV writes an object pronoun inside such a rendering — `וַיַּפֵּל` → *he let* ***it*** *fall*, `וַיַּשְׁקְ` → *gave* ***them*** *drink* — read whether an object morpheme is present. Where one is, it takes the pronoun under rule 18 and the verb keeps the rest, as in `וַיַּעֲבִירֵם` → *caused* ***them*** *to pass through*. Where none is, the pronoun answers to no morpheme, is its own `added` unit under rule 30, and does not join the verb merely because it stands inside its rendering; the verb's unit is discontinuous around it under rule 25. Position inside the English verb phrase is not what makes a word part of the verb's rendering — the complement is what the verb's lexeme is rendered by, and an object is not.
amendments.why: PSA.78 aligned this construction two ways with nothing in the source to license the difference: 78.15 marked the supplied *them* of *gave them drink* `added`, while 78.28 folded the supplied *it* of *he let it fall* into the verb's unit, both verbs being hiphil wayyiqtol forms carrying no object suffix. Rule 44's light-verb clause is what made the fold look defensible, since it says the head goes on the complement and says nothing about objects; the nearest guidance in the contract is rule 20's sentence about an object supplied alongside a supplied *lexical* verb, which does not reach a clause whose verb is Hebrew. The amendment states the division rule 44 was silent on, and states it where a verse pass reading rule 44 will meet it, rather than leaving the silent sentence in place behind a cross-reference. It is a narrow qualification: it changes nothing where an object suffix is present, which is the ordinary case (PSA.78.13, 78.53, 78.55), and it cites rules 18, 25 and 30 by number for the three dispositions it distinguishes.

conventions: Supplied English in this chapter divides on one line: an object pronoun the ASV writes for a verb that carries no object morpheme is its own added unit (78.4 them, 78.6 them twice, 78.15 them, 78.28 it, 78.38 their and them, 78.51 their, 78.59 this), including where it stands inside a causative or light-verb rendering; everything else the ASV supplies joins the morpheme that licenses it, namely the copula (78.9, 78.30, 78.35, 78.37, 78.38, 78.39, 78.57, 78.71), the subject pronoun and modal, the article and the indefinite article, the relative of an asyndetic relative clause (78.6, 78.8, 78.39, 78.54, 78.60, 78.65, 78.69) and the emphatic own written for a possessive suffix (78.29, 78.52).

A clause connective the ASV supplies is aligned to a waw only where that waw stands at the head of the clause the connective introduces: 78.20 and 78.53 so that, 78.31 When, 78.60 So that. Where the clause is asyndetic the connective is added, since no morpheme is there to carry it: 78.9 and between the coordinated participles, 78.40 And, 78.42 Nor, 78.44 so that. PSA.78.59 is the case that decides the rule rather than an exception to it: a waw is present, but at the head of the apodosis, while the ASV's When subordinates the preceding asyndetic clause, so the waw is unrepresented and the When is added.

An English preposition the ASV supplies only to attach a verb to its object stays in the verb's unit, discontinuously under rule 25, wherever the Hebrew verb governs its object directly: 78.1 Give ear ... to, 78.17 and 78.40 rebel against, 78.34 inquired after, 78.66 put ... to. Where the object marker is present it takes that word instead under rule 16, as at 78.56 rebelled against. Read whether a morpheme is there to carry the preposition before deciding which of the two it is.

report: One genuine cross-verse split, fixed in PSA.78.28. PSA.78.15 (wayyashq, rendered gave them drink) and PSA.78.28 (wayyappel, rendered he let it fall) are the same construction: a hiphil wayyiqtol carrying no object suffix, rendered by the ASV as a causative or light verb with a supplied object pronoun standing inside that rendering. 78.15 marked the supplied them added; 78.28 folded the supplied it into the verb's unit. Nothing in the source licenses the difference, so 78.28 is patched to give it its own added unit, leaving the verb's unit discontinuous under rule 25.

The chapter's treatment of supplied English is otherwise uniform, and that uniformity is what makes 78.28 the outlier rather than 78.15: supplied object pronouns are added in 78.4, 78.6 (twice), 78.15, 78.38 (twice), 78.51 and 78.59, while supplied copulas (78.9, 78.30, 78.35, 78.37, 78.38, 78.39, 78.57, 78.71), subject pronouns, articles, indefinite articles, relatives (78.6, 78.8, 78.39, 78.54, 78.60, 78.65, 78.69) and the emphatic own (78.29, 78.52) all join the morpheme that licenses them.

Checked and found consistent, the source licensing each difference: the assimilated article (all 25 follow whether the ASV writes a the, 15 aligned and 10 unrepresented); waw rendered also (78.14, 78.16, 78.27, 78.46, 78.48, 78.55, 78.62, 78.70, all aligned postpositively under rule 51); the object marker H853 (object written bare, so unrepresented, in 78.5, 78.42, 78.53 and 78.68 twice; rendered against in 78.56, which is rule 16's preposition family); the preposition bet left with nothing where the ASV promotes its object (78.59, 78.67 twice, 78.70); waw plus negative fused only where the ASV writes one word (78.37 Neither) and split in all nine other places; the rule 30 fusions (78.21, 78.23, 78.40, 78.53, 78.55, 78.70), each one English rendering; and the causative and light-verb head choices, which follow rule 44's subtraction throughout.

PSA.78.59 looks like a split with PSA.78.31 and is not one. In 78.31 the waw stands at the head of the very clause the ASV's When subordinates, so it takes that word; in 78.59 the waw stands at the head of the apodosis while the ASV's When subordinates the preceding asyndetic clause, so the waw is unrepresented and the When is added. The connective and the waw belong to different clauses there, which is why rule 51's postpositive reasoning does not reach it.

BSB: no genuine error among the 23 disagreements. Thirteen are the R class recurring across 12 verses, which is rule 40's documented convention difference; the rest are the paragogic he and nun of rule 32 (78.1, 78.44, and rule 32 names the Psalms as where this recurs), the object marker of rule 16 (78.53), and five places where the ASV simply writes no word at all: the interrogative particle realized by inversion (78.19, 78.20), the disjunctive im (78.20), the object suffixes of 78.3 and 78.69 where the ASV writes no object for known or established, and the suffix of adonay (78.65). None of these would be improved by moving an accepted edge.

Conventions: three recorded, covering the added-versus-folded line for supplied English, the treatment of clause connectives against asyndeton, and where an English preposition of verb government goes when no Hebrew preposition or object marker is present. The other 25 repeated notes in the validation report restate contract rules and are left unrecorded.

Contract: one amendment, to rule 44. Its light-verb clause is what made folding it into let it fall look defensible, and the rule says nothing about objects; rule 20 says the nearby thing only for an object supplied alongside a supplied verb. The qualification is added to rule 44 itself rather than returned as a new rule pointing back at it.
